lastError: Review rework needs a management decision after stagnation.
lastSummary: The delivered revision is a planning-only feasibility and decomposition record. It contains the intended comparison structure, names Phaser as the working recommendation pending validation, decomposes Increment A and Increment B with prerequisites, acceptance criteria, bounded capacity proposals and browser-verification plans, records an incompatibility escalation rule, states that no external deadline, budget or time constraint blocks the increment, and explicitly leaves package pinning, scaffolding, canvas, input, startup-baseline, QA and playtest work for future increments. It also avoids self-declared current artifact publication status and labels performance numbers as unmeasured guardrails rather than results. It cannot pass independent QA because the accepted-source traceability remains not independently verifiable from the supplied review evidence and the package/API technical-suitability evaluation is still all E0 with no version-pinned authoritative documentation or observed Chromium/build evidence supplied.

diagnostics: Resolve accepted-source index traceability before acceptance: provide reviewer-accessible content for the accepted source revisions c403bac5-45c7-4fd4-ad1d-6e979cef41d4 revision 5c14e28d-2617-4884-963f-9c2e344278f1 and 8f9c2c92-d2b0-4efd-ab2f-6e71e578e377 revision 2944885c-9282-45f5-93b5-754de6ee76cf, including the enumerated canonical source-index arrays and exact positions for the R1-R14 citations, or obtain a recorded accountable-owner amendment or waiver of the canonical Producer/Game-Director/Creative-Director source-index requirement. The current Appendix A local P, XP, G and ME registers plus verbatim anchors are useful but cannot be independently crosswalked to canonical source indexes from the supplied review evidence.

Supply independent technical-suitability evidence for the package comparison: attach version-pinned authoritative package documentation extracts for the exact resolved phaser 3.x, pixi.js v8, excalibur.js 0.x and Canvas 2D plus Web Audio APIs needed by V-01 through V-19, or attach observed Chromium/build test results from a named commit and package version. As delivered, every toolchain matrix cell is E0 and the document explicitly says no cell supports a suitability conclusion and no route is shown to satisfy all requirements, so the acceptance requirement to evaluate a technically suitable browser-package alternative is not independently verified.

If the intent is to accept the current matrix as planning-only rather than a technical-suitability evaluation, revise the artifact to separate candidate comparison questions from feasibility findings and obtain an accountable-owner amendment to the acceptance criterion requiring technical suitability. Do not treat E0 validation questions or proposed guardrails as feasibility or acceptance evidence.

criteria.criterion: A versioned platform artifact is published containing the feasibility/decomposition record and supporting material, and its content and source references are reviewed at that revision.
criteria.evidence: The platform metadata identifies the reviewed revision and the delivered content contains a feasibility/decomposition record, comparison material, escalation records, increment decomposition, source register Appendix A, and R-id mapping Appendix A2. However, the supplied reviewEvidence contains only accepted source artifact identifiers, not the underlying source bodies or enumerated source-index arrays. The artifact's Appendix A defines local P, XP, G, ME and G1.x registers and states that canonical Producer 0-22, Game-Director 23-37 and Creative-Director 38-352 index arrays are not present and ESC-02 remains open. Therefore the R-id source mappings cannot be independently checked at the canonical source-index level from the supplied review evidence.

criteria.criterion: The artifact evaluates Phaser and at least one technically suitable browser-package alternative against the accepted desktop-web browser-tab PoC constraints, Chromium-only verification target, fixed single-screen 2D canvas direction, mouse/keyboard input, required accessibility controls, and frozen non-goals, without claiming any package as approved.
criteria.evidence: The Toolchain Feasibility section provides a comparison matrix for phaser 3.x, pixi.js v8 plus custom loop, excalibur.js 0.x, and browser-native Canvas 2D plus Web Audio across the required constraint dimensions, and it states no package is approved, installed, pinned, selected, adopted or assumed. However, it also states that every matrix cell is E0, that no cell supports a suitability conclusion, and that no route is shown to satisfy all requirements. No version-pinned authoritative package documentation or observed Chromium/build test evidence is supplied in the review packet for the API or capability dimensions needed to independently verify that any alternative is technically suitable against the frozen constraints.

criteria.criterion: The artifact recommends one package candidate for engineer validation and states that Phaser remains the working recommendation unless infeasible; no engine replacement or alternative package is treated as approved or assumed.
criteria.evidence: The Toolchain Feasibility section explicitly names phaser (3.x line) as the working recommendation and the single candidate named for engineer validation, states that exact package name and version remain unresolved technical work, and states that no package is approved, installed, pinned, selected, adopted or assumed. It says Phaser remains first only as the lowest-authority-risk validation target and not a feasibility verdict, and that alternatives are comparison candidates only.

criteria.criterion: The artifact decomposes deferred engineer-owned increments, including dependency pin/lock/restore/version assertion/commit and fixed canvas/desktop-input startup baseline, with prerequisites, acceptance criteria, capacity need, and browser verification plan.
criteria.evidence: The Deferred Engineer-Owned Increments section defines Increment A for dependency pin, lock, restore, version assertion and commit, and Increment B for fixed canvas, desktop input and Chromium startup baseline. Each row records owner/reviewer, prerequisites, scope, acceptance criteria, browserVerification values none and canvas, a bounded capacity proposal of one game-engineer implementation increment after package selection and after Increment A, and why later work depends on it.

criteria.criterion: The artifact records that if accepted requirements become incompatible with all feasible browser packages, the precise conflict is raised as a feasibility decision rather than silently amended.
criteria.evidence: The Escalation, Incompatibility and Constraint Position section records a binding incompatibility rule. It states that if any accepted requirement R1 through R14 becomes incompatible with every feasible browser package, the record must not be silently amended or relaxed, and the precise conflict must be raised as an open feasibility decision naming the conflicting R-ids, source revisions and indexes, failed routes, V-ids, evidence class and required owner-authorized choice.

criteria.criterion: The artifact records that no external deadline, budget, or time constraint blocks this planning increment and missing dates do not block the capacity proposal.
criteria.evidence: The Constraint position section explicitly states that no external deadline, budget or time constraint blocks the planning increment, that missing dates do not block the capacity proposals, and that no date or effort figure is inferred. It also records Producer or management alone schedules capacity and recording a capacity need authorizes neither hiring nor spend.

criteria.criterion: The artifact explicitly leaves dependency pin/lock/restore/version assertion, scaffold, canvas, input, and startup baseline work to deferred engineer-owned increments and does not claim any such work is completed.
criteria.evidence: The Out of Scope and Non-Claims section explicitly states that package install or version resolution, lockfile creation or dependency restoration, repository inspection, commit or branch operation, scaffold, scene, canvas or input implementation, browser scenario harness, startup-baseline execution, browser evidence, QA, playtest, profiling, cross-browser matrix, real-device certification, deployment, hiring and spend were not performed, asserted or implied. The Deferred Engineer-Owned Increments section places the remaining pin/restore/version assertion and fixed canvas/input/startup-baseline work in Increment A and Increment B.

criteria.criterion: The feasibility review records that Phaser remains the working recommendation only until technical feasibility validates it, and that no alternative engine replacement is assumed or claimed as approved; if accepted requirements become incompatible with all feasible browser packages, that precise conflict is raised as an open feasibility decision rather than silently changed.
criteria.evidence: The Toolchain Feasibility section states that phaser remains the working recommendation and single validation candidate only until technical-feasibility validation confirms it, that no package is approved, installed, pinned, selected, adopted or assumed, and that removing Phaser from first position requires E2 or E3 failure against a named V-item and Director-level technical direction. The Escalation, Incompatibility and Constraint Position section and Approval Criteria Part 3 also record the incompatibility rule and state that, absent validation evidence, the record remains planning-only and Phaser remains the working recommendation pending validation.

criteria.criterion: The planning and feasibility baseline assumes no external deadline, budget, or time constraint, and missing dates do not block the increment or capacity proposal.
criteria.evidence: The Constraint position section states that the planning increment assumes no external deadline, budget or time constraint, that missing dates do not block the capacity proposals, and that no date or effort figure is inferred. Requirement register R11 also maps the accepted no-external-deadline and no-budget/time-constraint positions to cited anchors.
